messages.subject: Subsetting data with ggvis
parts:
Hi all,

I’m trying to create an interactive plot with ggvis. The idea is that it be a bar plot with a slider, which is manipulated to choose which subset of data to display. I can do this with ggplot and manipulate, but ggvis eludes me. A partial example is below. Anyone know how to do this?

testdata = structure(list(time = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.0339124038349837, 0.0339124038349837, 
0.0339124038349837, 0.0339124038349837, 0.0339124038349837, 0.0370037311994758, 
0.0370037311994758, 0.0370037311994758, 0.0370037311994758, 0.0370037311994758, 
0.20428497762613, 0.20428497762613, 0.20428497762613, 0.20428497762613, 
0.20428497762613), infections = c(0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 0L, 1L, 
2L, 3L, 4L, 0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L), population = c(100L, 
0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 99L, 1L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 98L, 2L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 97L, 
2L, 0L, 0L, 0L)), .Names = c("time", "infections", "population"
), row.names = c(1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 102L, 103L, 104L, 105L, 
106L, 203L, 204L, 205L, 206L, 207L, 304L, 305L, 306L, 307L, 308L
), class = "data.frame")

library(ggplot2)

#If I were to plot with ggplot, just selecting one slice in time, I would do this:
ggplot(subset(testdata, time < 0.01), aes(x=infections, y=population)) + 
    geom_bar(stat="identity")

library(manipulate)

#Using RStudio's `manipulate`, I can create a slider to select the time, but
#this only displays in RStudio
manipulate(
    ggplot(subset(testdata, time == max(testdata$time[testdata$time <= TIME])),
                 aes(x=infections, y=population)) + 
        geom_bar(stat="identity"),
    TIME = slider(min=0, max=max(testdata$time))
)

#Now I want to do the same with ggvis.  To make a static plot, I do this:
library(ggvis)
subset(testdata, time < 0.01) %>% 
  ggvis(~infections, ~population) %>%
    layer_bars()

# So how do I make a dynamic plot in ggvis?
​

Filter_.ggvis is what you need:

  # Dynamically restrict range using filter
     mtcars %>% ggvis(~disp, ~mpg) %>%
        filter(cyl > eval(input_slider(0, 10))) %>%
        layer_points()

messages.author: f8f554f3c8aec296
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Subsetting data with ggvis
parts:
Note for completeness you need dplyr loaded for some reason. Code below works with your testdata: 

 library(dplyr)
testdata %>%
 ggvis(~infections, ~population) %>%
 filter(time >= eval(input_slider(0, 0.05))) %>%
 layer_bars()
